package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion platform was compromised via a sophisticated supply chain attack, where attackers surreptitiously injected malicious code into the legitimate software build process. This resulted in the distribution of a trojanized DLL (SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll) within official updates, which deployed a covert backdoor (SUNBURST/Solorigate) to approximately 18,000 downstream customers, including critical US government agencies. The backdoor enabled persistent remote access, command execution, and lateral movement within affected networks.

execution_context.trigger: post-update installation, during normal Orion service runtime
execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (located in the Orion installation directory, trojanized within official update package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after update installation, the code checks if it is running within the SolarWinds.BusinessLayerHost process, establishes an outbound HTTP/S connection to the attacker-controlled domain avsvmcloud.com, receives remote commands from the C2 server, and executes those commands on the host system, resulting in covert remote access and arbitrary code execution by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces unauthorized remote command-and-control functionality by establishing persistent outbound connections to an attacker-controlled domain and executing arbitrary commands received over the network. This behavior is not present in legitimate SolarWinds Orion components and enables full compromise of the host.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion DLLs should not initiate unsolicited outbound connections to external domains unrelated to SolarWinds infrastructure, nor should they execute arbitrary code or commands received from the network. The presence of such logic in a core business layer DLL is a direct violation of expected software integrity and operational boundaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate network management software may contact official update servers or send telemetry to trusted SolarWinds endpoints, but it should never connect to unapproved external domains or execute remote code without explicit user authorization and auditability.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S connections from SolarWinds.BusinessLayerHost.exe to avsvmcloud.com (C2 domain) or similar attacker infrastructure
Presence of modified SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with malicious logic
Execution of arbitrary commands or code on the host system initiated by remote instructions
Stealthy operation within a legitimate, signed DLL to evade detection

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the SolarWinds Orion software build environment and injects malicious code into the SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll, creating a trojanized DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is embedded within the official SolarWinds Orion software update packages.

attack_chain.action: Customers download and install the compromised Orion update, deploying the trojanized DLL to their production systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious DLL is now present and loaded by the Orion platform on customer systems.

attack_chain.action: During normal operation, the trojanized DLL initiates covert outbound connections to the attacker's C2 domain (avsvmcloud.com), receives remote instructions, and executes arbitrary commands on the compromised system.
attack_chain.leads_to: The attacker gains persistent remote access and control, enabling further exploitation, lateral movement, and data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTP/S connections from SolarWinds.BusinessLayerHost.exe or related Orion processes to avsvmcloud.com or other known SUNBURST C2 domains
Orion DLLs or processes executing code or commands received from external network sources
Presence of previously unseen or modified SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll in the Orion installation directory
Unusual process injection or spawning of child processes by Orion services
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with a hash value not matching any official SolarWinds release
Unexpected modifications or additional exports in Orion platform DLLs
Timestamp anomalies or digital signature mismatches in Orion DLLs
network_indicators: Outbound connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 domains (e.g., digitalcollege.org, freescanonline.com, deftsecurity.com, thedoccloud.com)
Unusual HTTP/S traffic from Orion servers to external IP addresses or domains not associated with SolarWinds
Beaconing patterns consistent with SUNBURST (e.g., periodic, low-and-slow C2 traffic)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor Orion platform installations for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to known SUNBURST C2 domains such as avsvmcloud.com and related infrastructure. Validate the integrity of SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll and other core DLLs by comparing their hashes and digital signatures against official SolarWinds releases. Alert on any Orion process that executes code or commands received from the network, or that spawns unexpected child processes. Employ EDR, file integrity monitoring, and network traffic analysis to detect behavioral anomalies and unauthorized communications.
